Gattung.et: From Middle High German gatunge, from gaten (“to come together, to fit”), from Old High German (bi)gaton, from Proto-West Germanic *gadōn. Cognate with Dutch gading (“satisfaction”).

Gatte.et: From Middle High German gate, from Old High German *gato, from Proto-West Germanic *gadō, from Proto-Germanic *gadô (“comrade”); related to Proto-West Germanic *gaduling (“relative, kinsman”). Akin to Old Saxon gigado, Old High German gatuling. Cognate to Dutc…

Gatter.et: From Middle High German gater, from Old High German gataro.

Gate.et: Borrowed from English gate, ultimately Proto-Germanic *gatą. Doublet of regional Gatt (“hole, eye”), from Low German. Probably also related with inherited Gasse (“lane”).
Borrowed from Hungarian gatya, from Serbo-Croatian gaće (“underpants”).

s: eyelet; hole for a rope or hook
Gatt.et: Borrowed from Middle Low German gat, from Proto-Germanic *gatą. Cognate with Dutch gat, English gate. Doublet of Gate.

Gatsch.et: From regional Early New High German gatsch, gätsch, getsch (“dung, sludge, thick mush”), further origin unknown.
